 Officers Get A Call About Mesh Tunnel In Yard And Find 4 'Soaking Wet' Babies Inside
 “[They were] freezing, covered in fleas and beyond confused …”
 By Maeve Dunigan Published on Oct 23, 2026 at 11:24 AM Earlier this month, the Asbury Park Police Department received an anonymous tip about a group of abandoned pets struggling to survive in a suburban yard.
 Officers rushed to the scene with members of Monmouth County SPCA ’s animal control team. When they arrived, they found a mesh play tunnel draped over a concrete wall. Inside, four cats cowered in fear, their fluffy coats soaked through after hours of waiting in the rain.
 Monmouth County SPCA Officers couldn’t believe their eyes.
 “Seeing something like this is always devastating for us,” Monmouth County SPCA media and marketing manager Lindsay Sanator told The Dodo. “It’s impossible to understand how anyone could abandon an animal like that.”
 Monmouth County SPCA The rescuers gently grabbed each cat, placed them inside their vehicle and brought them to the SPCA for further care.
 “[They were] soaking wet, freezing, covered in fleas and beyond confused about what was happening to them,” the SPCA wrote in a Facebook post .
 Monmouth County SPCA Expert staff gave the cats a full examination. Today, the cats are up to date on initial vaccines, receiving flea and tick treatment and enjoying regular meals. Once their stray hold ends, they’ll be available for adoption and start looking for permanent families.
 Monmouth County SPCA Rescuers say the cats are “desperate” for love and affection. They look forward to the day when they're all safe in their forever homes.
 “These cats are very friendly,” the SPCA wrote. “We have no doubt that when they're ready for adoption, they'll find good homes in no time.”
 To help other animals like these cats, you can donate to Monmouth County SPCA .  Related Related Woman Follows ‘Strange Noises’ To Dumpster And Finds Tiny Soul Living In Diaper Box
